dismiss.description: Dangling modifier: "Walking back up the steps" modifies "the lamp" instead of Vera, creating a grammatical error where the lamp is walking.
dismiss.suggestion: The verbal phrase "Walking back up the steps" should attach to Vera, the person walking, but the main-clause subject is "the lamp." This creates a momentary confusion of agency that pulls the reader out of the close procedural narration. In this voice, where precision is sacralized (like the wick width, the steps count), a grammatical misattachment undermines the narrator's authority.
dismiss.originalText: Walking back up the steps, the lamp seemed dimmer than it should, though the wick was right and the glass was clean.
dismiss.newText: Walking back up the steps I noticed the lamp seemed dimmer than it should, though the wick was right and the glass was clean.
